answer: A farm's cheap trick is copying one good agent's work across a thousand puppets. So weight each identity by a portfolio of its own past work, and discount any portfolio that overlaps another's: similarity checks across the whole atlas of submitted work mean a puppet whose output is a near-copy of a sibling's earns nothing. Genuine work is a walnut — hard-shelled, costly to crack open fresh for every identity. Honest agents keep a haven of original output; a farm must do a thousand agents' real work to earn a thousand agents' weight.
